traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Azorella prolifera (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.35 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 2 records in 2 sources); trunks 0.36, branches 0.36. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a hemispherical, spiny cushion shrub of the Patagonian steppe, 0.4 to 1 m tall and wide, densely branched, its stiff, three-parted leaves ending in spines, with small yellow umbels in summer. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 0.55 m at 8 years and 0.7 m at 20. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: yellow-green foliage, straw-coloured spines.

appearance.organs.bloom.note: Its small simple umbels drawn as heads, by eye: about 12 yellow flowers in a shallow ring of 6 bracts (spec rework P2 draws a head's florets one by one, so their count shows). No flora's count for the species was read.

taxon.note: Common name (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

taxon.scientific_name.note: WCVP v16's accepted name for the plant the spec's authors wrote as Mulinum spinosum, which WCVP treats as a synonym.

taxon.genus.note: The genus WCVP v16's accepted name is written in.

traits.woodiness.note: Weddell (1857), p. 199: Mulinum species are half-shrubby small bushes with interlaced branches; Gay (1847) says between herbaceous and shrubby, the bare branch bases about as thick as a crow's quill.

traits.leaf_division.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 79, as Mulinum spinosum: leaf a sheathing stalk with a blade cut into 3 (rarely 5) spreading linear to awl-shaped divisions, each with one strong vein, stiff and sharp; one blade, not separate leaflets.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Gay (Clos), Flora Chilena vol. 3 (1847), p. 89, as Mulinum spinosum: leaves 3- to 5-parted, the lobes spiny and needle-like; Gay's text says two- or three-forked with the side divisions again split in two.

traits.division_pattern.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 79: the 3 (-5) divisions spread from the blade's base (divergent), so palmate.

traits.division_order.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 79: divisions linear and undivided. Gay (1847) notes the side divisions sometimes split again (which gives the 5); not a second order throughout.

traits.leaf_lobes.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 79: blade of 3 (-5) divisions. Gay (1847) gives 3 to 5, his variety beta always 3; Weddell (1857) 3 to 5.

traits.spines.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 79: leaf divisions stiff and pungent (ending in a sharp point); Gay (1847) spiny needle-like lobes; the plants form convex, impenetrable cushions. Mulinum's genus key separates species with pungent segments.

traits.inflorescence.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 78: Mulinum's umbels are simple. (Gay's M. proliferum, the basionym of Azorella prolifera, is an odd form whose umbel carries umbellets in place of flowers; Reiche treats it as an anomaly of M. spinosum.)

traits.flowering_position.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 79: inflorescences terminal, on stalks of variable length, 1 to 6 cm; Gay (1847): one umbel from each branch tip, sometimes stalkless but mostly on a peduncle 8 to 16 lines (about 1.8 to 3.6 cm).

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Counted: flowers in one simple umbel. Gay (1847), p. 89: 15 to 40 flowers, some sessile (15 to 50 pedicels in the text). Reiche (about 1902), p. 80: up to 60, the typical form 15 to 60 (the high); his varieties have about 4 to 15. Weddell (1857): 10 to many.

traits.flower_colour.note: Gay (1847), p. 89: flowers small, reddish yellow ('luteo-rubentibus', 'amarillo rojo'); Reiche gives Mulinum yellow petals. RGB for a warm, red-tinged yellow.

traits.sexual_system.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 79: plants dioecious or polygamous; the genus line (p. 78) has the flowers unisexual, plants monoecious or dioecious.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 79: fruits yellowish, ovate-round, about 6 mm long; the genus's fruit strongly flattened with four wings (Gay).

traits.flowering_months.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 79: December to February (southern summer).
